rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when someone gives reasons for an action, including explaining their own decision without necessarily arguing aggressively.

example.english: I can justify why I am not going to work today.
example.traditional: 我可以解釋點解今日唔返工。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ho2 ji5 gaai2 sik1 dim2 gaai2 gam1 jat6 m4 faan1 gung1

rows.note: Use this when the speaker is actively defending a questionable action or trying to prove that someone is in the right.

example.english: You are still trying to justify him, even though he clearly messed things up.
example.traditional: 你仲要為佢辯護，明明係佢搞爛件事喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 zung6 jiu3 wai6 keoi5 bin6 wu6 ming4 ming4 hai6 keoi5 gaau2 laan6 gin6 si6 wo3

rows.note: Use this only for arranging text so that its left and right edges line up on a page or screen.

example.english: You need to justify the text left and right so it looks good when printed.
example.traditional: 呢份文件啲字要左右對齊，印出嚟先好睇。
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 man4 gin6 di1 zi6 jiu3 zo2 jau2 deoi3 cai4 jan3 ceot1 lai4 sin1 hou2 tai2
